div.head: II Cn 2a
div.ab: ⁊ geþence swyþe georne se ðe domes geweald áge, hwæs he sylf gyrne, þonne he þus cweðe: 'Et dimitte nobis debita nostra sicut et nos dimittimus.' (þæt is on Englisc: '⁊ forgyf us, Drihten, ure gyltas, swa we forgyfað þam ðe wið us agyltað').
⁊ geþence swyðe georne se ðe domes geweald age, hwæs he sylf georne, þonne he þus cweð: ‘Et dimitte nobis debita nostra, sicut et nos dimittimus’.
And geþence swiðe georne se ðe domes geweald áge, hwæt he æt us sylf gyrne, þonne he þus cweðe: ‘Et dimitte nobis debita nostra, sicut & nos dimittimus’.

Et multa sedulitate cogitet qui ius habet in iudicio, quid sibi postulet á Domino, dicens: ‘Dimitte nobis debita nostra, sicut et nos dimittimus’ (et ‘Non intres in iudicium cum seruo tuo, Domine, quia non iustificabitur in conspectu tuo omnis uiuens’).
⁊ geðence swiðe georne se ðe domes geweald áge hwæs he sylf gyrnne, ðonne he ðus cweðe: "Et dimitte nobis debita nostra sicut et nos dimittimus."

And geþence swyþe georne se ðe domes geweald age hwæs he sylf gyrne þonne he þus cweðe: Et dimitte nobis debita nostra, sicut et nos dimittimus; þæt is on Englisc: “and forgyf us, Drihten, ure gyltas, swa we forgyfað þam ðe wið us agyltað.”

Und es bedenke recht ernstlich, wer die Amtsgewalt des Richterspruches hat, was er selbst begehrt (von uns D), wenn er folgendermassen spricht: ‘Et dimitte nobis debita nostra, sicut et nos dimittimus’ (das heisst auf Englisch: ‘und vergieb uns, Herr, unsere Verschuldungen, wie wir vergeben denen, die uns gegenüber sich verschulden’ G).

And let whoever has the power of judgment consider very earnestly what he himself desires (from us, D) when he says: ‘And forgive us our debts, as we forgive’ (that is in English: ‘and forgive us, Lord, our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us’, G).
And he who has authority to give judgment shall consider very earnestly what he himself desires when he says thus: "and forgive us our trespasses as we forgive [them that trespass against us]."

And the person who has the power to pass judgment shall reflect sincerely upon his own motivations when he recites thus: Forgive us our trespasses as we forgive those who trespass against us, that is in English, “Forgive us, Lord, our trespasses as we forgive those who trespass against us.”

div.note: G's English rendering of the Latin (‘þæt is on Englisc …’) is in G alone and not original (Liebermann; compare VI Atr 10.2). Quadr.'s ‘Non intres in iudicium …’ (Ps. 142:2) is probably a gloss added in the first edition. Liebermann compares VI Atr 10.3.
Forgive us our trespasses . . . against us: Luke 11:4.
